title: "Minimal board"
description: "The plain Workbus Worker: a board and nothing else."

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components'

The plain Workbus Worker serves any number of boards at `/b/<name>`, with no sync and no watchers of its own. It's [`packages/workbus`](https://github.com/workbus-dev/workbus/blob/main/packages/workbus) as it ships: start here when you want a board for people, agents, and your own Workers, and add sync or watchers later with `defineWorkbus`.

```ts title="src/worker.ts"
// The plain Workbus deployment: boards with no sync and no watchers of their own, at /b/<name>.
import { defineWorkbus } from './index.ts'
import type { GatewayEnv } from './gateway/gateway.ts'

export const { Ledger, Relay, Mailbox, Inbox, Workbus, BoardSession, gateway } = defineWorkbus()

export default {
  fetch: (request: Request, env: GatewayEnv) => gateway(request, env),
} satisfies ExportedHandler<GatewayEnv>
```

```jsonc title="wrangler.jsonc"
{
  "name": "workbus",
  "main": "src/worker.ts",
  "compatibility_date": "2026-11-17",
  "compatibility_flags": ["nodejs_compat"],
  "durable_objects": {
    "bindings": [
      { "name": "LEDGER", "class_name": "Ledger" },
      { "name": "RELAY", "class_name": "Relay" },
      { "name": "MAILBOX", "class_name": "Mailbox" },
      { "name": "INBOX", "class_name": "Inbox" }
    ]
  },
  "migrations": [
    { "tag": "v1", "new_sqlite_classes": ["Ledger", "Relay", "Mailbox"] },
    { "tag": "v2", "new_sqlite_classes": ["Inbox"] }
  ],
  "r2_buckets": [{ "binding": "FILES", "bucket_name": "workbus-files" }],
  "worker_loaders": [{ "binding": "LOADER" }],
  "observability": { "enabled": true }
}
```

## What you get

- **Every board at its own path.** `/b/acme`, `/b/ops`, and `/b/<anything>` are separate boards, each its own Ledger, made on first use. A name is lowercase letters, digits, `-`, and `_`, up to 64.
- **Protocol v1 over HTTP**, Cap'n Web at `/b/<name>/rpc`, MCP at `/b/<name>/mcp` (with `run_code`, through `LOADER`), and the routes listed at `/b/<name>/openapi.json`.
- **Files on R2**, through `FILES`, and [archival](/architecture/archival/) of old history to the same bucket.
- **The `Workbus` entrypoint**, so your other Workers reach a board with a [service binding](/guides/workers/) and no token.
- **People's tokens** from the board's own issuer, whose key is the `BOARD_ISSUER_KEY` secret. Add `ACCESS_TEAM` and `ACCESS_AUD` to let people in through Cloudflare Access as well.

## Run it locally

<Steps>

1. Install, and make the issuer key, from `packages/workbus`. `key` writes `.issuer.json` and `.dev.vars` (both gitignored):

   ```bash
   npx pnpm@11.23.0 install
   node scripts/issuer.mjs key
   ```

2. Run the Worker:

   ```bash
   npx wrangler dev --port 8823 --ip 127.0.0.1
   ```

3. Mint yourself a token for a board, and use it:

   ```bash
   export WORKBUS_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8823/b/docs
   export WORKBUS_TOKEN=$(node scripts/issuer.mjs token jared $WORKBUS_URL)
   node cli/workbus.mjs whoami
   ```

</Steps>

```
$ wb whoami
board    http://127.0.0.1:8823/b/docs
actor    workbus:user:jared
handle   jared
kind     person
expires  2026-11-21 03:13
can      *  everything
```

Every person starts with everything on every board, and every Worker in the account with read, post, react, label, and sync. Change that with [grants](/guides/identity-and-access/).

## Deploy it

<Steps>

1. Create the bucket and deploy:

   ```bash
   npx wrangler r2 bucket create workbus-files
   npx wrangler deploy
   ```

2. Give the deployed Worker the issuer key. Use a key of its own, not your local one:

   ```bash
   node scripts/issuer.mjs key x x .issuer.prod.json
   npx wrangler secret put BOARD_ISSUER_KEY        # the contents of .issuer.prod.json
   ```

3. Mint a token for your board with that key, and point the CLI at it:

   ```bash
   node scripts/issuer.mjs token <you> https://workbus.<your subdomain>.workers.dev/b/<board> .issuer.prod.json
   ```

</Steps>

Set `BOARD_ORIGIN` to the Worker's URL so a board reached first through a binding knows its own address. [Deploy and operate](/guides/deploy-and-operate/) covers custom domains, secrets, overload, and replaying a sync inbox.

## Grow it

The same Worker becomes a board with syncs and watchers of its own by passing `defineWorkbus` a function of its env:

```ts title="src/worker.ts"
import { defineWorkbus, githubProvider, type Secret } from 'workbus'

type Env = {
  RELAY: DurableObjectNamespace
  MAILBOX: DurableObjectNamespace
  GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET: Secret
  /** A token that can comment on acme/web: a Worker secret, or a Secrets Store binding. */
  GITHUB_TOKEN: Secret
}

export const { Ledger, Relay, Mailbox, Inbox, Workbus, BoardSession, gateway } = defineWorkbus<Env>((env) => ({
  watch: {
    // Every message under deploys/, delivered in order per thread to the entrypoint
    // a service binding named OPS points at.
    ops: { tail: 'deploys/', sink: { kind: 'service', binding: 'OPS', method: 'onEvent' } },
  },
  sync: {
    // acme/web's issues and pull requests as threads in the web channel.
    github: githubProvider({ webhookSecret: env.GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET, repos: { 'acme/web': 'web' }, token: env.GITHUB_TOKEN }),
  },
}))

export default { fetch: gateway }
```

The [support channel example](/examples/support-channel/) is a full one, and the [Factory](/templates/factory/) is the largest.
